intro: These Books are called by the Greek interpreters, Paralipomenon, that is, of things left out, or omitted; because they are a kind of a supplement of such things as were passed over in the books of the Kings. The Hebrews call them Dibre Haijamim, that is, The words of the days, or The Chronicles.--Not that they are the books which are so often quoted in the Kings, under the title of the words of the days of the kings of Israel, and of the kings of Juda: for the books of Paralipomenon were written after the books of Kings: but because in all probability they have been abridged from those ancient words of the days, by Esdras or some other sacred writer.

chapters.1: The genealogy of the patriarchs down to Abraham: The posterity of Abraham and of Esau.
chapters.2: The twelve tribes of Israel. The genealogy of Juda down to David. Other genealogies of the tribe of Juda.
chapters.3: The genealogy of the house of David.
chapters.4: Other genealogies of Juda and Simeon, and their victories.
chapters.5: Genealogies of Ruben and Gad: their victories over the Agarites: their captivity.
chapters.6: The genealogies of Levi, and of Aaron: the cities of the Levites.
chapters.7: Genealogies of Issachar, Benjamin, Nephtali, Manasses, Ephraim, and Aser.
chapters.8: The posterity of Benjamin is further declared down to Saul. His issue.
chapters.9: The Israelites, priests, and Levites, who first dwelt in Jerusalem after the captivity. A repetition of the genealogy of Saul.
chapters.10: Saul is slain for his sins: he is buried by the men of Jabes.
chapters.11: David is made king. He taketh the castle of Sion. A catalogue of his valiant men.
chapters.12: Who followed David when he fled from Saul. And who came to Hebron to make him king.
chapters.13: The ark is brought from Cariathiarim. Oza for touching it is struck dead.
chapters.14: David's house, and children: his victories over the Philistines.
chapters.15: The ark is brought into the city of David, with great solemnity. Michol derideth David's devotion.
chapters.16: The ark is placed in the tabernacle. Sacrifice is offered. David blesseth the people, disposeth the offices of Levites, and maketh a psalm of praise to God.
chapters.17: David's purpose to build a temple, is rewarded by most ample promises: David's thanksgiving.
chapters.19: The Ammonites abuse David's ambassadors: both they and their confederates are overthrown.
chapters.20: Rabba is taken. Other victories over the Philistines.
chapters.21: David's sin in numbering the people is punished by a pestilence: which ceaseth upon his offering sacrifice in the thrashingfloor of Ornan.
chapters.22: David having prepared all necessaries, chargeth Solomon to build the temple and the princes to assist him.
chapters.23: David appointeth Solomon king. The distribution of the Levites and their offices.
chapters.24: The divisions of the priests into four and twenty courses, to serve in the temple: the chiefs of the Levites.
chapters.25: The number and divisions of the musicians.
chapters.26: The divisions of the porters. Offices of other Levites.
chapters.27: The twelve captains for every month; the twelve princes of the tribes. David's several officers.
chapters.28: David's speech, in a solemn assembly: his exhortation to Solomon. He giveth him a pattern of the temple.
chapters.29: David by word and example encourageth the princes to contribute liberally to the building of the temple. His thanksgiving, prayer, and sacrifices: his death.

notes: Concubine... She was his lawful wife, but of an inferior degree.
Achar... Alias Achan. Jos. 7.-Ibid. The anathema... The thing devoted or accursed, viz., the spoils of Jericho.

Ram... He is commonly called Aram. But it is to be observed here, once for all, that it was a common thing among the Hebrews for the same persons to have different names: and that it is not impossible among so many proper names, as here occur in the first nine chapters of this book, that the transcribers of the ancient Hebrew copies may have made some slips in the orthography.
Caleb... Alias Calubi, ver. 9.
He that saw, etc... The Latin interpreter seems to have given us here, instead of the proper names, the meaning of those names in the Hebrew. He has done in like manner, ver. 55.
The concubines... The inferior wives.
Six... Counting the father in the number.
Jabes... That is, sorrowful.

He that made, etc... Viz., Joazim, the meaning of whose name in Hebrew is, he that made the sun to stand. In like manner the following names, Lying (Chozeba), Secure (Joas), and Burning (Saraph), are substituted in place of the Hebrew names of the same signification.
Plantations and Hedges... These are the proper names of the places where they dwelt. In Hebrew Atharim and Gadira.
Accounted to Joseph... Viz., as to the double portion, which belonged to the firstborn; but the princely dignity was given to Juda, and the priesthood to Levi.
Beria... This name signifies in evil, or in affliction.
Esbaal... Alias Isboseth.
Meribbaal... Alias Miphiboseth. 2 Kings 4.4.
Nathineans... These were the posterity of the Gabaonites, whose office was to bring wood, water, etc., for the service of the temple.
Two ariels... That is, two lions, or lion-like men; for Ariel in Hebrew signifies a lion.
The prophecy, to give out the tunes... Singing praises to God is here called prophecy: the more, because these singers were often inspired men.
Seven thousand chariots... That is, of men who fought in chariots.

The number, etc... The difference of the numbers here and 2 Kings 24. is to be accounted for, by supposing the greater number to be that which was really found, and the lesser to be that which Joab gave in.

Three years famine... Which joined with the three foregoing years of famine mentioned, 2 Kings 21. and the seventh year of the land's resting, would make up the seven years proposed by the prophet, 2 Kings 24.13.
Ornan... Otherwise Areuna.
Six hundred sicles, etc... This was the price of the whole place, on which the temple was afterwards built; but the price of the oxen was fifty sicles of silver. 2 Kings 24.24.
He had not a firstborn... That is, his firstborn was either dead or not fit to be chief; and therefore he made Semri the chief.
Holy vessels... Or vessels of the holy places, or of things holy. Vasa sanctorum.
